scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapter 1: A two-period model. The last day and the two-period fiscal-theory equilibrium (existence and uniqueness of the price level given surpluses, for any expectation system); monetary and fiscal policy: share splits, interest-rate targets and the Fisherian response, the expected/unexpected inflation decomposition; debt sales and Table 1.1 (borrow, inflate, AR(1), s-shaped surpluses) with the borrowing condition corrected; a price-level target rule; active versus passive policy, the gamma-rule determinacy condition corrected, non-identification and observational equivalence; links to Woodford's locally Ricardian policy and Ricardian transversality results.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapter 1, pp. 4-19.
